claims.statement: The product is melody-in-heart (applicationId cn.com.dcsgo.mihx), a purely local offline-first Android music player with no INTERNET permission, running Kotlin 2.0.21 + Compose (BOM 2025.09.01) + Media3 1.9.0 (with Jellyfin FFmpeg decoder) + Hilt 2.52 + Room 2.6.1 + DataStore 1.1.1 + WorkManager 2.9.1 + LiteRT 1.4.1, at versionName 3.11.0 / versionCode 46, minSdk 33, targetSdk 36, Java 11 bytecode, split into 15 Gradle modules (:app, :core:model, :core:common, :core:ui, :core:skin, :domain, :data, :player, six :feature:* modules, :benchmark).

verifyProductArchitecture is a Gradle task registered in the root build.gradle.kts verification group and wired into the root check lifecycle; since m-10 (2026-10-15) the rule body lives in buildSrc as pure logic (ProductArchitectureVerification.verify(rootDir) returning all violations at once, unit-tested by ProductArchitectureVerificationTest) rather than an inline doLast block. It statically asserts module boundaries (no :data/:player/cross-feature deps from features, no implementation-layer import leaks, no :core:model Android resources/UI resource ids, MusicRepository kept as an internal coordinator bound via narrow adapters), the Hilt entry points and DI modules, immutable Room schema snapshots (incl. locked v1/v2/v3), LazyColumn stable keys, AppLog over android.util.Log, no stale cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.data.player package references, release R8/resource-shrink settings, privacy backup excludes, no READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE, no startup-path permission requests, and no Android Things references; a GradleException reports every violated rule.

./gradlew check aggregates the root spotlessCheck, the root verifyProductArchitecture, and every one of the 14 subprojects' own check tasks (each subproject's check also depends on its spotlessCheck covering Kotlin/Kotlin-script/XML formatting); it must be run before committing.

CLAUDE.md and docs/ are valuable but historically lagging references that must be cross-checked against code: as of v3.11.0 CLAUDE.md's version table matches the catalog (Compose BOM 2025.09.01, Kotlin 2.0.21 with the built-in org.jetbrains.kotlin.plugin.compose compiler, and the old composeOptions { kotlinCompilerExtensionVersion } block is gone), but its Room status comment still reads 'Schema export data/schemas/ (当前 v10)' while code is now MelodyDatabase v11 with 14 entities; source and tests are the only authority.

The 15-module layering is: :app shell (AppRoot/AppNavHost/AppRoutes, PermissionCoordinator, emotion scan worker, shell/skin resolver, app-level Hilt modules) depends on all other modules; six :feature:* modules depend only on :core:* and :domain and expose the Route+Screen pattern; :domain holds repository interfaces plus pure playback policy with no Android dependencies; :data owns Room MelodyDatabase and DataStore wrappers with narrow adapters; :player owns AppMediaSessionService, PlaybackController, windowed queue planning, Bluetooth coordination, and EmotionAnalyzer support; :core:model/common/ui hold pure data types, logging/trace, and shared Compose components, and :core:skin holds the skin description model, parser and fail-closed validation.

Offline and privacy invariants: the app manifest declares POST_NOTIFICATIONS, FOREGROUND_SERVICE, FOREGROUND_SERVICE_MEDIA_PLAYBACK and BLUETOOTH_CONNECT with no INTERNET permission; READ_MEDIA_AUDIO is accepted solely to accelerate the import scan (fast java.io.File traversal when already granted) while SAF document-tree access remains the primary/fallback path, and verifyProductArchitecture forbids READ_EXTERNAL_STORAGE and bans startup-path requests for notification/Bluetooth/READ_MEDIA_AUDIO permissions (only user-triggered Settings paths may request); backup/data-extraction rules must exclude playback state, Room files, DataStore files, and the album-art cache.

Room persistence is MelodyDatabase v11 with 14 entity classes (songs, playlists, playlist-song cross-ref, play stats, playback events, quick-skip songs, quick-skip short plays, song group overrides, migration state, artists, albums, song-artist cross-ref, song_emotions, word_preferences) and exportSchema=true with JSON snapshots 1.json..11.json under data/schemas/; DatabaseModule registers MelodyMigrations.ALL (extracted to the public object MelodyMigrations for regression-test reuse, covering MIGRATION_1_2 through MIGRATION_10_11) and provides SharedPreferencesLegacyJsonMigration for the first-launch v1 SharedPreferences-JSON-to-Room migration; historical schema JSON must never be edited.

Five DataStore preference files complement Room: player_settings (theme, play modes, Bluetooth/notification toggles, lyric font scale, sleep timer, emotion scan pause, mood-time-slot master switch), playback_state (playback snapshot persistence, owned by :player's PlaybackStateStore with a legacy music_player_prefs SharedPreferences), playlist_resume (per-playlist resume JSON), mood_time_slot (time-slot configs as a single-key JSONArray), and emotion_failures (per-song failure JSON with attempts counting); all are excluded from backup.

Emotion batch scanning is scheduled from MelodyApplication.onCreate via EmotionScanScheduler as a WorkManager unique periodic work (emotion_periodic_scan) every 6 hours under charging + battery-not-low constraints with a 30-minute initial delay and NetworkType.NOT_REQUIRED; the periodic EmotionScanWorker analyzes up to 40 pending songs per run while the manual trigger (manual=true one-time work, unique name emotion_manual_scan) analyzes up to 300 per run and auto-enqueues the next batch with APPEND semantics.

EmotionAnalyzer (cn.com.dcsgo.mihx.player, @Singleton) uses FfmpegPcmDecoder (a MediaExtractor + Jellyfin FFmpeg decoder driving the same media3 extension used for playback, chosen after a MediaCodec vendor-soft-decode SIGSEGV on some ROMs) to decode mono s16 PCM, resamples to 16 kHz, then runs per-window YAMNet + emotion_va_head.tflite in :player assets (model version yamnet-va-v3, 5s window / 2.5s hop) producing valence/arousal curves and whole-song mean; both decoder and analyzer share a memory budget derived from maxMemory() to deterministically truncate high-sample-rate tracks instead of OOM, failures carry a displayable EmotionFailureReason, are persisted to EmotionFailureStore, and songs accumulating MAX_ATTEMPTS=3 failures stop being auto-retried.

Analysis results persist in the Room song_emotions table (SongEmotionEntity: valence, arousal, curveJson of raw per-window [v,a,...] floats, peakSec, windowsAnalyzed, durationSec, modelVersion, analyzedAt, plus base64 1024-dim embeddingB64 and userValence/userArousal/userTags calibration fields) through SongEmotionsRepository implementing the :domain SongEmotionRepository interface.

Mood time-slot semantics: MoodSlotResolver (:domain, pure logic, independently unit-tested) treats configs as left-closed/right-open [start, end) intervals with end <= start meaning cross-midnight, picks the earliest-starting hit on overlap, and validates saves returning SlotValidation (empty name/name too long/no tags/zero-length/conflict) which TimeSlotConfigStore throws as IllegalArgumentException; PlayerRandomQueueFacade evaluates the active slot per random-play request and filters candidates by emotion tags at the planner entry, falling back to full-library random when the filtered pool is empty and warning when it is below MoodSlotPolicy.POOL_WARN_THRESHOLD=10.

PlayerViewModel is a deliberately thin @HiltViewModel facade delegating to PlayerRuntime, a composition root injected via PlayerRuntimeFactory that lazily assembles graph objects (PlayerQueueGraph, PlayerMediaControllerGraph, PlayerPersistenceGraph, PlayerBluetoothGraph, PlayerPlaybackSessionGraph) and ~16 per-concern facades (library, import, playlist, song-deletion, quick-skip, controller-queue, queue, controller-state, playback, media-event, version, random-queue, lifecycle, error, playback-bridge, startup); the old PlayerViewModelComponents assembly hub was deliberately dismantled and verifyProductArchitecture fails the build if any file references it again.

Queue invariants: PlayQueue.songs is the full business queue (duplicates allowed; currentIndex indexes into it) while MediaController only holds a windowed plan whose size stays between 51 and 71 items (20 before + current + 50 after, clipped at queue edges) for 100/500/1000-song libraries as locked by PlaybackWindowPerformanceShapeTest; SongMediaItemMapper sets MediaItem.mediaId to Song.id.toString() as the mapping contract back to the business queue; navigation goes through MediaController, not PlayQueue index arithmetic.

Build variants: debug (no minification, applicationIdSuffix .debug so it coexists with release), release (R8 minify + resource shrink, arm64-v8a only, resConfigs zh/en, falls back to debug signing without keystore.properties unless -PrequireReleaseSigning=true makes the build fail), and benchmark (initWith release but debug-signed, non-debuggable, adds x86_64 for emulators); :benchmark is an Android-test (com.android.test) module targeting :app with StartupBenchmark (cold-start StartupTimingMetric, with and without a baseline profile) and ScrollBenchmark (FrameTimingMetric) run via :benchmark:connectedCheck.

Navigation: AppRoutes defines the Navigation Compose route table (home, playlist, playlist/{id}, artist/{name}, album/{name}, user, settings, lyrics, playback-stats, song-top-list, version-management, emotion-analysis, mood-time-slot, skin-switcher, etc.); the former compile-time AppDestinations enum of three fixed bottom tabs was replaced in the P2 shell rework by an AppShell whose tabs come from the active skin, with AppShell.fromTabRoute/currentDefaultTab reproducing AppDestinations.fromRoute sub-page-to-tab attribution so tab highlight stays correct; app-shell ViewModels including MoodTimeSlotViewModel must be created at Activity scope in AppRoot, because creating them inside NavHost composable blocks falls back to a non-Hilt factory and crashes.

Test tiers: JVM unit tests (./gradlew test, no device) live in domain/, player/, data/, feature/*/, core/* (including core/skin parser/validation) and app/ test sourcesets covering planners, synchronizers, repositories, facades, and skin/shell resolution; instrumented Compose tests (HomeScreenComposeTest, PlaylistScreenComposeTest, SettingsScreenComposeTest, RuntimePermissionPolicyTest) run via :app:connectedAndroidTest on an emulator/device; Macrobenchmarks run via :benchmark:connectedCheck with EMULATOR suppression for x86_64 simulators, though MIUI ROMs may block them.

The Room word-preference feature (v3.11.0): a new word_preferences table (WordPreferenceEntity with word PK, likeVotes, dislikeVotes, updatedAt), a MIGRATION_10_11 creating it registered in MelodyMigrations.ALL, the :domain WordPreferenceRepository interface (observeAll/getAll/recordSongOutcome/clearAll) backed by :data WordPreferencesRepository, and the WordPreference.kind majority-vote classification (LIKE/DISLIKE/NEUTRAL) in :core:model; votes are counted on song settle via PlayerRuntime.handleExploreSongSettled calling recordSongOutcome. The domain ExplorePlaybackPolicy defines INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE=10, REFILL_COUNT=5, REFILL_THRESHOLD=0, MIN_LISTEN_MS=30000, MIN_LISTEN_RATIO=0.25 and isSkipped() as the pure completion-vs-skip judgment shared with the vote counting.

Explore play (探索播放) is a distinct RandomEnhanceMode (OFF/TIME_SLOT/EXPLORE, mutually exclusive with TIME_SLOT) surfaced on :feature:player via playerSettingsRepository.randomEnhanceMode: PlayerRandomQueueFacade.playRandomQueue generates ExplorePlaybackPolicy.INITIAL_BATCH_SIZE=10 songs and sets isExplorePlay (disabling infinite random), refillExplorePlayQueue adds REFILL_COUNT=5 songs when REFILL_THRESHOLD songs remain, and buildExploreRefillPool tiers candidates by liked-and-no-dislike → only-no-dislike → full library using WordPreference.kind; PlayerRuntime observes the mode to set isExploreModeActive and exits the explore session when the mode leaves EXPLORE.
